acceptance_criteria.criterion: getInstance() returns the same instance on repeated calls.
getAll() returns IconInfo[] sorted alphabetically by ID.
getCustomIcons() returns only icons where isCustom() is true.
getStandardIcons() returns only icons where isStandard() is true.
getByID() returns the correct IconInfo for a known icon ID.
idExists() returns false for non-existent IDs.
When a custom icon has the same ID as a standard icon, the custom icon replaces it.

summary: Created src/classes/UI/Icons/IconCollection.php — a singleton registry in the UI\\Icons namespace. The constructor calls a private loadIcons() method that parses APP_INSTALL_FOLDER/themes/default/icons.json via JSONFile::factory(), then optionally loads APP_ROOT/themes/custom-icons.json if it exists. Each icon ID is normalised (hyphens/spaces → underscores) via a private normaliseID() method. Custom icons with the same ID as a standard icon replace the standard entry (array key overwrite). All icons are sorted alphabetically by ID via ksort(). Provides getAll() (array_values of the sorted map), getStandardIcons() and getCustomIcons() (filter loops), getByID() (array lookup with RuntimeException on miss), idExists() (isset check), and countIcons(). PHPStan clean — only pre-existing DBHelper/FetchMany.php error present. composer dump-autoload completed. Existing 2 IconsTests pass with no regressions.

comments.note: getByID() throws a plain RuntimeException for unknown IDs rather than a domain-specific exception. This is acceptable given the current absence of a UI\\Icons exception class, but a dedicated IconCollectionException would make error handling more granular for callers in a future WP.

The singleton instance (self::$instance) is never reset, which is standard for production use but makes unit-testing the load path harder (no way to force a reload after injecting a different APP_ROOT/APP_INSTALL_FOLDER constant value). A package-scoped or test-only reset hook (e.g. a static resetInstance() marked @internal) could ease test isolation. Not required for current scope.

IconCollection::loadFromFile() silently skips a missing file (returns void after !$file->exists() check). This is intentional for custom-icons.json (optional), but if the framework icons.json were missing the collection would silently be empty. A log warning or a more explicit error on missing required JSON would improve observability.

comments.note: No IconCollectionTest.php was created. All 7 ACs were verified by bootstrap execution and code inspection, but there is no persistent automated test for the IconCollection class. getByID() does not normalize the caller's input ID before lookup. Callers must pass the underscore form (e.g. 'time_tracker') not the raw JSON key ('time-tracker'). This is not an AC violation but could be a foot-gun. Consider documenting this in the method docblock or adding input normalization.

AC 7 (custom replaces standard) was verified by code-path inspection only. The test environment's custom-icons.json contains only new IDs ('planet', 'revisionable') — not an override of any standard icon. The override code path ($this->icons[$id] overwrite) is correct, but no end-to-end test fixture exercises the actual replacement scenario.

comments.note: Expanded getByID() docblock to document the ID normalisation precondition. The original docblock omitted any mention that the $iconID parameter must be in normalised form (underscores, not hyphens/spaces). Callers passing 'time-tracker' instead of 'time_tracker' would receive a RuntimeException with no hint as to why. Added @note, updated @param description, and added @throws annotation. Non-behavioral change; QA validation remains intact.

The file_exists($customPath) guard in loadIcons() is redundant — loadFromFile() already handles missing files via !$file->exists(). Could be simplified to call loadFromFile($customPath, true) unconditionally. Not applied (structural change belongs to a future cleanup WP) but worth noting for maintainability.

getByID() does not normalise its input. Callers passing raw JSON keys (e.g. 'time-tracker') will receive a RuntimeException rather than the expected icon. Input normalisation in getByID() would make the API more forgiving but that is a behavioral change — deferred to a future WP. Docblock now documents the precondition.

loadFromFile() silently swallows a missing standard icons.json (the required framework data source). If APP_INSTALL_FOLDER/themes/default/icons.json were absent, the collection would be silently empty. A warning log or explicit error for the non-optional path would improve observability. Flagged as low-priority technical debt by Developer; no change needed now.
